passages.text: In that day the LORD will take His sharp, great, and mighty sword, and bring judgment on Leviathan the fleeing serpent —Leviathan the coiling serpent—and He will slay the dragon of the sea.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the holy and powerful God.
He will act on a special day.
On that day, the LORD will use His sword.
His sword is sharp.
His sword is great.
His sword is mighty.
The LORD will judge Leviathan.
Leviathan is a fleeing serpent.
Leviathan is also a twisting serpent.
The LORD will also kill the dragon in the sea.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָה֩ בְּחַרְב֨וֹ הַקָּשָׁ֜ה וְהַגְּדוֹלָ֣ה וְהַֽחֲזָקָ֗ה עַ֤ל לִוְיָתָן֙ נָחָ֣שׁ בָּרִ֔חַ וְעַל֙ לִוְיָתָ֔ן נָחָ֖שׁ עֲקַלָּת֑וֹן וְהָרַ֥ג אֶת־ הַתַּנִּ֖ין אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּיָּֽם׃ס

passages.text: In that day: “Sing about a fruitful vineyard.
passages.sermon:
God is speaking.
God commands people to sing.
God tells them to sing about a vineyard.
This vineyard is fruitful.
This vineyard is precious.
passages.original: בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד עַנּוּ־ לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: I, the LORD, am its keeper; I water it continually. I guard it night and day so no one can disturb it; I am not angry. If only thorns and briers confronted Me, I would march and trample them, I would burn them to the ground.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the keeper of the vineyard.
The LORD watches over the vineyard.
The LORD waters the vineyard all the time.
The LORD guards the vineyard every night and every day.
No one can disturb the vineyard.
The LORD is not angry.
If thorns and briers come against the LORD,
The LORD will march against them.
The LORD will trample them.
The LORD will burn them together.
passages.original: אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ לִרְגָעִ֖ים אַשְׁקֶ֑נָּה פֶּ֚ן יִפְקֹ֣ד עָלֶ֔יהָ לַ֥יְלָה וָי֖וֹם אֶצֳּרֶֽנָּה׃ חֵמָ֖ה אֵ֣ין לִ֑י מִֽי־ יִתְּנֵ֜נִי שָׁמִ֥יר שַׁ֙יִת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה אֶפְשְׂעָ֥ה בָ֖הּ אֲצִיתֶ֥נָּה יָּֽחַד׃

passages.text: Or let them lay claim to My protection; let them make peace with Me— yes, let them make peace with Me.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God offers His protection.
Anyone may take hold of God's strength.
They can seek safety in Him.
They can make peace with God.
Yes, they can make peace with Him.
passages.original: א֚וֹ יַחֲזֵ֣ק בְּמָעוּזִּ֔י יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה שָׁל֖וֹם לִ֑י שָׁל֖וֹם יַֽעֲשֶׂה־ לִּֽי׃

passages.text: In the days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.
passages.sermon:
Jacob is the ancestor of Israel.
Jacob’s descendants are the people of Israel.
In the future, Jacob’s descendants will take root.
Israel will grow.
Israel will blossom.
Israel will produce fruit.
Israel’s fruit will fill the whole world.
passages.original: הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב יָצִ֥יץ וּפָרַ֖ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמָלְא֥וּ פְנֵי־ תֵבֵ֖ל תְּנוּבָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Has the LORD struck Israel as He struck her oppressors? Was she killed like those who slayed her?
passages.sermon: The LORD punished Israel.\r\nHe did not strike Israel as He struck Israel’s oppressors.\r\nThe LORD did not kill Israel as He killed those who killed Israel.
passages.original: הַכְּמַכַּ֥ת מַכֵּ֖הוּ הִכָּ֑הוּ אִם־ כְּהֶ֥רֶג הֲרֻגָ֖יו הֹרָֽג׃

passages.text: By warfare and exile You contended with her and removed her with a fierce wind, as on the day the east wind blows.
passages.sermon:
God fought against Israel.
God used war to contend with Israel.
God sent Israel away into exile.
God removed Israel with His strong wind.
God’s wind was fierce, like the east wind on a stormy day.
passages.original: בְּסַּאסְּאָ֖ה בְּשַׁלְחָ֣הּ תְּרִיבֶ֑נָּה הָגָ֛ה בְּרוּח֥וֹ הַקָּשָׁ֖ה בְּי֥וֹם קָדִֽים׃

passages.text: Therefore Jacob’s guilt will be atoned for, and the full fruit of the removal of his sin will be this: When he makes all the altar stones like crushed bits of chalk, no Asherah poles or incense altars will remain standing.
passages.sermon:
Jacob is the ancestor of Israel.
Jacob sinned.
God will atone for Jacob’s guilt.
God will remove Jacob’s sin.
This is the result of removing his sin.
Jacob will destroy all the altar stones.
He will crush the altar stones like bits of chalk.
No Asherah poles will remain standing.
No incense altars will remain standing.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן בְּזֹאת֙ יְכֻפַּ֣ר עֲוֺֽן־ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְזֶ֕ה כָּל־ פְּרִ֖י הָסִ֣ר חַטָּאת֑וֹ בְּשׂוּמ֣וֹ׀ כָּל־ אַבְנֵ֣י מִזְבֵּ֗חַ כְּאַבְנֵי־ גִר֙ מְנֻפָּצ֔וֹת לֹֽא־ יָקֻ֥מוּ אֲשֵׁרִ֖ים וְחַמָּנִֽים׃

passages.text: For the fortified city lies deserted— a homestead abandoned, a wilderness forsaken. There the calves graze, and there they lie down; they strip its branches bare.
passages.sermon:
A fortified city stands empty.
No one lives there.
People have abandoned their homes.
The city is like a wilderness.
Calves walk there.
Calves lie down in the empty place.
The calves eat all the branches.
They leave nothing behind.
passages.original: כִּ֣י עִ֤יר בְּצוּרָה֙ בָּדָ֔ד נָוֶ֕ה מְשֻׁלָּ֥ח וְנֶעֱזָ֖ב כַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר שָׁ֣ם יִרְעֶ֥ה עֵ֛גֶל וְשָׁ֥ם יִרְבָּ֖ץ וְכִלָּ֥ה סְעִפֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: When its limbs are dry, they are broken off. Women come and use them for kindling; for this is a people without understanding. Therefore their Maker has no compassion on them, and their Creator shows them no favor.
passages.sermon:
This people does not have understanding.
Their branches dry up.
Their limbs break off.
Women come.
Women use the broken branches for kindling.
God made this people.
God is their Creator.
God does not have compassion on them.
God does not show them favor.
passages.original: בִּיבֹ֤שׁ קְצִירָהּ֙ תִּשָּׁבַ֔רְנָה נָשִׁ֕ים בָּא֖וֹת מְאִיר֣וֹת אוֹתָ֑הּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א עַם־ בִּינוֹת֙ ה֔וּא עַל־ כֵּן֙ לֹֽא־ יְרַחֲמֶ֣נּוּ עֹשֵׂ֔הוּ וְיֹצְר֖וֹ לֹ֥א יְחֻנֶּֽנּוּ׃ס

passages.text: In that day the LORD will thresh from the flowing Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt, and you, O Israelites, will be gathered one by one.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
He is powerful and acts with purpose.
On that day, the LORD will act.
He will thresh from the Euphrates River to the Wadi of Egypt.
He will gather the people of Israel.
He will gather them one by one.
No one will be forgotten.
Each Israelite will be brought together by the LORD.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יַחְבֹּ֧ט יְהוָ֛ה מִשִּׁבֹּ֥לֶת הַנָּהָ֖ר עַד־ נַ֣חַל מִצְרָ֑יִם וְאַתֶּ֧ם תְּלֻקְּט֛וּ לְאַחַ֥ד אֶחָ֖ד בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: And in that day a great ram’s horn will sound, and those who were perishing in Assyria will come forth with those who were exiles in Egypt. And they will worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
He will act on a special day.
On that day, a great ram’s horn will sound.
People who were lost in Assyria will come.
People who were exiled in Egypt will also come.
They will gather together in Jerusalem.
They will worship the LORD.
They will worship Him on His holy mountain.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִתָּקַע֮ בְּשׁוֹפָ֣ר גָּדוֹל֒ וּבָ֗אוּ הָאֹֽבְדִים֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְהַנִּדָּחִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהִשְׁתַּחֲו֧וּ לַיהוָ֛ה בְּהַ֥ר הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
